summary: This PR introduces layout restructuring and adds debug logging. The most serious issue is the removal of `relative` positioning from the main element in page.tsx, which breaks absolute positioning of background elements and navigation. Multiple debug console.log statements have been added to production code, and a test file with only console.log was committed.

accepted.title: Missing 'relative' on main element breaks absolute positioning
accepted.message: The main element lost the 'relative' class (was present in L53). Background blur elements (absolute top-0/bottom-0) and the navigation (absolute right-6 top-1/2) now position relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (likely body/html) instead of the main container, causing visual misplacement.
accepted.suggestion: Add 'relative' back to the main className: className="relative h-screen w-full bg-[#060812] overflow-hidden"

accepted.title: Test file with only debug logging committed
accepted.message: A new file testing.ts was added containing only console.log("apple"). This appears to be a leftover test artifact that should not be in the codebase.

accepted.title: Debug console.log left in production proxy handler
accepted.message: A console.log statement was added to the proxy function that logs every request with timestamp and URL. This creates noise in production logs and could expose request URLs.
accepted.suggestion: Remove the console.log line or guard it with a development environment check.

accepted.title: Debug console.log left in Home component render
accepted.message: A console.log statement logs on every render of the Home component with a timestamp. This will spam the console in production and impact performance.
